title: Do Models Agree on Calibration? Shared Overconfidence as a Correlated Failure

original_idea.body:
# Do Models Agree on Calibration? Shared Overconfidence as a Correlated Failure

**Problem:** Correlated errors are studied as shared wrong ANSWERS, but shared overconfidence (all models confidently wrong on the same items) is distinct and underexplored.

**Direction:** Elicit answers and verbalized confidence from ~10 models on a safety QA set. Identify items where models are jointly wrong AND jointly high-confidence. Measure whether overconfident errors are MORE correlated than ordinary errors.

**Why it matters:** Many safety pipelines abstain/escalate based on confidence; if overconfidence is shared, those guardrails fail together.

**Relevant context:** Correlated Errors (arXiv:2506.07962); Great Models Think Alike (arXiv:2502.04313).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: shared overconfidence breaks confidence-based abstention/escalation guardrails uniformly, a concrete failure of a common safety mechanism.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: QA plus verbalized/token-prob confidence and correlation analysis; accessible with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: are overconfident errors more correlated than ordinary errors; clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models/data, no lab access; guardrail-fragility evidence labs underpublish.

novelty.reasoning: Shared overconfidence is a distinct, under-explored facet of correlated errors.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Correlated errors studied; shared-overconfidence facet less directly measured.
